previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with long-standing type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, gastroparesis, and bilateral foot ulcers was admitted for asymptomatic hyperkalemia with a potassium level of 6.2. The elevation was likely due to recent up-titration of losartan and mild acute kidney injury from reduced oral intake. She received intravenous insulin and fluids, which normalized her potassium and renal function. Her foot ulcers were healing well on continued oral antibiotics, and her blood glucose was stabilized on her home insulin regimen. Losartan was discontinued, and she was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider for blood pressure management and repeat potassium monitoring.
